questions.question: My stool test for colon cancer came back positive last November. Has a colonoscopy been scheduled, and if not, can we book it now?
questions.why: A positive stool blood test needs a follow-up colonoscopy, ideally within a few months; nearly a year later her records show no colonoscopy.

facts.says: Fecal immunochemical test (FIT) for blood in the stool was positive.

absences.what: No colonoscopy or other follow-up procedure after the positive FIT.
absences.coverage: All procedures in her records from Cascade North Demo Hospital (records retrieved 2024-02-01, 2025-02-01 and 2026-10-15); the only procedure is a chest CT angiogram on 2025-07-08.

knowledge.says: A positive FIT is an abnormal screening result, not a completed screen; a diagnostic colonoscopy should follow, ideally within 6 months, because delays beyond that are linked to more advanced cancer at diagnosis.
knowledge.guideline: US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer (2017/2025); USPSTF colorectal cancer screening (2021)

questions.question: My cholesterol was last checked before I started atorvastatin. Can we recheck it to see whether the statin is working?
questions.why: Her only lipid panel predates the statin started in February 2025; no follow-up panel shows whether her LDL has come down.

facts.says: LDL cholesterol was 131 mg/dL.
Total cholesterol was 212 mg/dL.
Atorvastatin 20 mg was prescribed and is active.

absences.what: No LDL or lipid panel after atorvastatin was started.
absences.coverage: All LDL results in her records from Cascade North Demo Hospital, 2023-07 through 2026-02; only the 2025-02-18 value exists.

knowledge.says: After starting a statin, a fasting or non-fasting lipid panel 4-12 weeks later checks response and adherence, then every 3-12 months as needed; in diabetes the LDL goal is under 100 mg/dL (under 70 with higher risk).
knowledge.guideline: 2018 AHA/ACC Cholesterol Guideline; ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2025, section 10

questions.question: Should I have a urine test for protein (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio) to check my kidneys for diabetes damage?
